about: Front lines of the Battle of Verdun, traced from the dated maps in battle-maps.json into Lambert-93 metres (EPSG:2154), each drawn west to east with its side, date and the map it was traced from. scripts/trace-front-line.py traces a line printed in its own ink; `checked` says what it was compared with.

lines.note: The German first line on the left bank, from the Bois de Malancourt to the Meuse below Forges. Printed on the 6 March map; it stood here from before 21 February until the left-bank attack of 6 March.
lines.checked: Avocourt, Malancourt, Haucourt, Béthincourt and Forges lie on the French side, Cuisy, Montfaucon, Septsarges and Gercourt on the German; the French held the slopes north of the Forges brook, Béthincourt and the Bois de Forges the points of contact (chtimiste.com, lesfrancaisaverdun-1916.fr).

lines.note: The German first line on the right bank on 21 February, from the Meuse by Consenvoye to the Woëvre by Gincrey, where the sheet ends.
lines.checked: Haumont, the Bois des Caures, Ornes, Maucourt and Mogeville lie on the French side; Consenvoye, Flabas, Ville-devant-Chaumont, Azannes, Gremilly and Gincrey on the German (the woods of Haumont, Caures, Ville and Herbebois were the French first line: Wikipedia, Battle of Bois des Caures).

lines.note: The French first line on the left bank, from the Bois d'Avocourt by Malancourt and the slopes north of the Forges brook to Forges and the Meuse. Printed on the 6 March map, as it stood until that day's attack.
lines.checked: Traced along the red French trenches nearest the German first line, 89% of its length on the ink. Never crosses the German line; no-man's land 150 m to 1.2 km wide, 400 m at the median. Avocourt, Malancourt, Haucourt and Béthincourt lie behind it, Cuisy, Montfaucon, Septsarges and Gercourt beyond.

lines.note: The French first line on the right bank on 21 February: Brabant, the woods of Haumont, the Caures and Ville, Herbebois, Ornes, Maucourt, Mogeville and Morgemoulin by Fromezey. In the woods a chain of posts more than a trench; the trace runs between them.
lines.checked: Traced along the red French trenches nearest the German first line, 69% of its length on the ink, the rest between separate posts. Never crosses the German line; no-man's land 250 m to 1.2 km wide, 740 m at the median, widest in the Woëvre. Haumont, Samogneux, Beaumont, Ornes and Bezonvaux lie behind it; Flabas, Ville-devant-Chaumont, Azannes, Gremilly and Gincrey beyond (the woods of Haumont, the Caures, Ville and Herbebois were the French first line: Wikipedia, Battle of Bois des Caures).

lines.note: The German first line on the right bank on 2 April: from the Meuse at Vacherauville along the Côte du Poivre, below Fort Douaumont and Vaux village, round Damloup and down the edge of the Woëvre past Eix and Moulainville to Châtillon-sous-les-Côtes.
lines.checked: Traced from the sheet's heavy blue 'first German line'. Douaumont, Vaux, Bezonvaux, Louvemont, Dieppe, Moranville and Abaucourt lie behind it; Bras, Fleury, Eix, Moulainville and Châtillon in front (Fort Douaumont fell on 25 February, Vaux village in March: Wikipedia, Battle of Verdun).

lines.note: The French first line on the right bank on 2 April, facing the German: the Côte du Poivre's south slope, the Bois de Nawé, Thiaumont, the Bois de la Caillette, below Fort de Vaux, Damloup, Eix, Moulainville and Châtillon.
lines.checked: Traced along the red French trenches nearest the German first line, 81% of its length on the ink. Never crosses the German line; no-man's land 130 m to 1 km, 410 m at the median.

lines.note: The German first line on the left bank on 20 June: from the Bois de Malancourt and the Bois d'Avocourt (taken 20 March) along the Tranchée des Aunes to the Bec de Canard, the Tranchées d'Aix and Vailly below Côte 304, over the Mort-Homme's crest and down to the Meuse south of Cumières.
lines.checked: Printed in a slate blue too dark to tell from the base map by colour, so followed along waypoints read by eye from the sheet. Malancourt, Haucourt, Béthincourt and Cumières (taken March to May) lie behind it; Avocourt, Esnes, Chattancourt and Marre in front.

lines.note: The French first line on the left bank on 20 June: the Tranchée du Golfe above Avocourt, the Réduit d'Avocourt, Côte 304's south slopes (Bec de Canard, Tranchées Brocart, Salle and Reboul), the Mort-Homme's south slope and the Ouvrage des Zouaves to the Meuse.
lines.checked: Traced along the red 'first French line', waypoints read by eye. Never crosses the German line; the lines are 60 to 500 m apart, 270 m at the median, closest on Côte 304 and the Mort-Homme.
